correctness.rationale: The sign projections commute with the Laplacian and restriction and separate the one-dimensional Walsh lines. For 0<|I|<d, take a in I and b outside I: the real part of (x_a+i x_b)^(2m+1) has parity odd in a and even in b and gives the nonzero odd-angle cosine times the a sign. The remaining |I|-1 distinct linear factors use disjoint coordinates. For the constant line, the harmonic quadratic has mean equal to its zero trace divided by d; in degrees divisible by four the planar even power has nonzero constant evaluation, and in degrees 6 mod 4 the displayed zonal degree-six polynomial has zero Laplacian and cube value 6/d^3, with any degree increment obtained by multiplying a planar harmonic on separate coordinates. The top character occurs at d by the squarefree product; at d+2 its parity projection is that product times a diagonal quadratic, whose trace must vanish because its Laplacian is six times the sum of coefficients times the squarefree product. On the cube this same sum controls the evaluation. Orthogonality, binomial rank and parity saturation then follow including degree zero and the three saturating degrees. Exact replay independently evaluates the kernel by rational recurrence and directly differentiates the degree-six witness; it passed all 505 tests. The proof, not this finite range, establishes all d in scope.
residual_risks: Exact demonstration concerns single-degree evaluations on the normalized sign cube; no conditioning claim or further degree range is inferred in this review.
